fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Three Ways Water Designs in Ice", "body": "Veda has studied water for nine and a half years, specialising in crystallography at the subtle stage between liquid and solid that Gerald Pollack calls the fourth phase of water and that she calls the state of creation. Opening the freezer after about five minutes and draining off the liquid layer, she finds water designing in three ways: signature patterns that repeat for tap, spring, rain and filtered water; art, since she says art is the heart of water; and hydroglyphs. When she circulated 25 ice photographs in an anonymous online survey, she reports, 85 percent of respondents recognised what each sample had been exposed to before freezing."}, {"title": "Fifty Repeats Before a Symbol Counts", "body": "A hydroglyph, in Veda's definition, is a symbol in ice that is both recognisable and repeatable. The idea took shape with Stairway to Heaven: after playing the song beside her petri dish about twelve times she kept seeing a stairway shape, so she wrote the word stairway, set the dish on it for thirty seconds, and has now seen that shape more than fifty times. Because every glyph must repeat fifty times, four and a half years have produced only 36. Days of the week refused to render, she says, and the one time frame water has given her is before and after Easter, a date set by the moon."}, {"title": "Water as a Witness, Not a Judge", "body": "Veda's father is Māori, and she notes that the Māori word for spirit, wairua, means two waters, the physical and the spiritual, both of which she believes we carry. The more she observes, the more the spiritual side of water seems a witness that does not judge. That conviction was tested when her teenage son, who liked neither classical music nor heavy metal, saw Masaru Emoto's contrasting images and worried that the water hated him. She told him water's nature is not to judge, then began freezing samples set beside every genre of music, and says water cares more about what you feel than what you think."}, {"title": "Did the First Alphabets Come From Ice", "body": "Chance argues that the savior figure found across traditions is credited with giving humanity its letters and that versions of him carry water in their names, Bacchus among them. He notes the Etruscans called their gods by a name with the word ice inside it, and wonders whether ice taught people their first flowing, curving alphabets. Veda answers that when she asked water what a hydroglyph is, it replied in hydroglyphs, calling them living messages. She recalls a dream, years before this work began, of an arched ice tunnel in Antarctica lined with shapes like an ancient script, and the talk turns to emojis as the hieroglyphs of today."}, {"title": "Light, Dreams and Life Beyond the Body", "body": "Veda describes water as mostly photons, a liquid light, and calls people liquid crystal solar panels. For three months she left a petri dish of water by her bed and froze it on waking, and she says the ice images often jogged her memory of dreams she had forgotten, which she links to astral travel and remote viewing. She cites three near death interviewees who each described watching their own resuscitation without attachment, and an experiment Pollack presented in which water in a chicken's body kept flowing for up to an hour after its heart was stopped. Chance closes by wondering whether, if water holds memory, blood does too."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Water isn't just a resource; it’s a living library. What if the water you drink is actually reflecting your thoughts, your dreams, and the very structure of your soul?
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: Veda Austin joins Chance Garton to unveil her groundbreaking research into "Hydroglyphs", recognizable and repeatable symbols that she says show water has memory. From the "Fourth Phase" of water to its mysterious connection to ancient alphabets and the human biofield, we dive into the fluid intelligence that connects all life.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Crop Circles and the Living Rosetta Stone", "body": "The members only hour opens with Chance asking whether hydroglyphs might share a grammar with crop circles, and Veda answers that she has already begun building a hydroglyph for the words crop circle, repeating it twelve times and seeing the same hexagonal shape with a small round dot beside it. She frames water as a kind of Rosetta Stone, a living picture language that could eventually let us read symbols nobody here authored. She extends the same idea to a Dalmatian in Devon whose drinking water carried its thoughts, and to a nonverbal child whose recorded sounds produced readable glyphs."}, {"title": "Water Will Not Design for a Dishonest Heart", "body": "Veda describes a boundary she did not expect to find. Water, she says, simply will not resonate with anger, frustration or manipulation. When she comes home irritated and tries to work anyway, the ice thickens, darkens and refuses to render complex imagery, though sadness is met differently and sad faces appear without judgment. Asked once whether she could deliberately trick the water, she promised it a private picture while privately intending to post it to thousands of followers, and nothing formed at all. What water reads, she concludes, is not your thought but your energy, and you cannot hide from it."}, {"title": "Three Hours Missing and the Lights Above the Bay", "body": "Veda shares a story she says she has told publicly only once. Riding horses as a girl, she waded off a New Zealand beach, felt something close around her ankle and was pulled under. Her body was missing for three hours before it was found and she was resuscitated, with no memory at all of what happened. Hypnotherapy years later produced a recorded account of a bioluminescent being that felt to her like a brother, a soundless vortex, and lights circling above a small bay off the coast of New York. Checked afterward, the date matched one of the most widely recorded UFO sightings."}, {"title": "Solar Archeology and Fire on the Water", "body": "About ten years ago Veda began writing material she had no prior knowledge of, which she insists was not channeling but a well of knowledge surfacing from within. The result is an unpublished book she calls solar archeology, covering platonic solids, junk DNA, and vats of salt water set inside pyramids lined with a pink stone, where men and women stood on either side with their hands on the rim until a crackling sound ignited a lightning like fire on the surface and the capstone lifted. Chance ties it to an old priestly conception of the Creator as liquid fire."}, {"title": "Atlantis, the Ego Meter and the First Mer People", "body": "Veda's Atlantis is a working machine, a central water wheel with the concentric rings turning around it like an atom, functioning as an atomic clock, and she places a parallel pair of civilizations in Antarctica, builders and mappers, the mappers making great circular devices that served both as timepieces and as ships. From there she tells of twins born to the priestess Halima whose tuning crystals kept shattering, of a scientist who built a crude meter for ego frequency and found that time in the ocean lowered it, and of the beings who left for the sea and became the first mer people."}]
